candidates.name: Maiden's Tower
candidates.content: One of the icons of the city is also called the Leander's Tower, on a Bosphorus islet off Salacak. The local myth ascribes its name to a princess, whose father wanted to protect her in this offshore tower from a prophecy that she

candidates.name: Beylerbeyi Palace
candidates.content: Bling palace-cum-summer house in mid-19th-century Ottoman style. Notable for its reception hall, bathing pavilion, and second floor restroom with spectacular Bosphorus view. Visit by guided tour only, these start every half-hour.

candidates.name: Dolmabahce Palace
candidates.price: Foreigners pay 1200 TL for Selamlık + Harem + Painting Museum, Domestic Visitors 170 TL, Müzeumkart not accepted
candidates.content: This lavish palace with 285 rooms and 43 halls was the admin centre for the Ottoman Empire in its last 60 years. The palace government block (Selamlık) includes the Imperial Mabeyn (State Apartments) and Muayede Hall (Ceremonial H

candidates.name: Yıldız Palace
candidates.hours: 08:00–19:00 during summer, and till 17:00 during winter
candidates.content: A vast complex of former imperial Ottoman pavilions and villas in Istanbul, Turkey, built in the 19th and early 20th centuries. It was used as a residence by the Sultan and his court in the late 19th century.

candidates.name: Rumeli Fortress
candidates.content: Built in first half of the 15th century, this is the large medieval castle under the Second Bosphorus Bridge. Its former name Boğazkesen (Turkish)/Laimokopia (Greek) means both "strait-blocker" and "throat-cutter" in both language

candidates.name: Sakıp Sabancı Museum
candidates.hours: Tue Thu Fri Sun 10:00-18:00; Wed Sat 10:00-22:00
candidates.content: Museum with a rich collection of calligraphy and paintings. It also hosts temporary exhibitions of works by some world-class artists such as Pablo Picasso from time to time.

candidates.name: Sadberk Hanım Museum
candidates.content: A private museum housed in a yalı, the traditional wooden waterfront mansions that line the banks of the Bosphorus. The exhibition includes a number of archaeological and ethnographical artifacts from the collection of the long-ti

candidates.name: Yusuf Ziya Mansion
candidates.content: It houses the headquarters of Borusan Holding and the Borusan Contemporary art museum. The popular nickname of the mansion, Perili Köşk (meaning the "Haunted Mansion") refers to its construction remaining partially unfinished for

candidates.name: Galata Tower
candidates.content: It was built by the Genoese in the 14th century on the city walls of Galata, marking the highest point of their territory. Ride an elevator and take two flights of stairs to the top, then walk the parapet for a 360°-view of Istanb

candidates.name: Galata Convent of Whirling Dervishes
candidates.content: A ritual dancing hall of the mystical Mevlevi order, the followers of the teachings of Mewlānā Rumi. The quiet and peaceful garden is a welcome escape from the hustle and bustle of Beyoğlu. The oldest Mevlevi lodge in Istanbul, th

candidates.name: Crimean Memorial Church
candidates.price: Free but 10 TL donation is requested for maintenance of the church
candidates.content: A neo-gothic Anglican cathedral which would not be out of place in northwestern Europe, the Crimean Memorial Church was built for the Protestant community of the city by Britain in the late 19th century. It was named in honour of

candidates.name: Pera Museum
candidates.price: 20 TL, concession 10 TL, free on Fridays 18:00–22:00, students free on Wednesdays
candidates.content: A private museum with a large painting collection and archaeological collections of measurement units and tools used in Asia Minor since antiquity and faiences of Kütahya.

candidates.name: S. Antonio di Padova Catholic Church
candidates.content: Although not at the size of Hagia Sophia, this is the largest active church in Turkey. It’s directly on Istiklal St, but somewhat hidden from view by its yard portal. Catholic Masses in Italian, Turkish, and English (in different

candidates.name: Museum of Innocence
candidates.price: 40 TL, 30 TL students, free admission on presentation of the novel
candidates.content: Opened in 2012, this museum is unique and a must-see when you are in the Beyoğlu area. It was created by Turkish Nobel laureate Orhan Pamuk alongside a novel of the same name. It tells the love story of the two main characters fro

candidates.name: Adam Mickiewicz Museum
candidates.content: A historic house museum dedicated to the life of Adam Mickiewicz, renowned Polish poet. This is where he lived while in Turkey from September 1855 to 26 November 1855, when he died of illness.

candidates.name: Miniaturk
candidates.content: It was built in 2001 and is the first miniature park in Istanbul (the world's largest miniature park in respect to its model area). The park hosts icons of many cultures and civilizations. Models vary from the Hagia Sophia to Gala

candidates.name: Aynalıkavak Pavilion
candidates.price: 90 TL; concessions for students and domestic visitors
candidates.hours: 09:00-17:00 (Closed Mon); you have to join the guided tours starting every 30 minutes in the high-season, and you may have all the place to yourself and the guide in winter
candidates.content: Started in 1613 by the Ottoman sultan Ahmet I (r. 1603–1617, who also had the Blue Mosque in the Old City built), and extensively renovated by the art-loving Selim III (r. 1789–1807), this sole building, which itself has the disti

candidates.name: Rahmi M. Koç Industrial Museum
candidates.price: 600 TL (July 2024, about €17); concessions for students and domestic visitors
candidates.content: This is an industry museum showcasing the evolution of machines. Many transport related items including a submarine, classic cars, railway carriages, an out-of-service Bosphorus ferry and a Douglas DC-3 aircraft (possible to board

candidates.name: Santral İstanbul
candidates.content: A contemporary art museum in a building converted from an old power plant: 1914-built and coal-fired, this was the oldest in Istanbul and the Ottoman Empire. Part of the plant was kept in almost exact original condition and now se

candidates.name: Hagia Sophia
candidates.content: The third and grandest of the churches on this site, completed in 537 AD. The 30-m diameter dome covers what was for over 1000 years the largest enclosed space in the world, only surpassed in 1520 by Seville cathedral. It used "pe

candidates.name: Topkapı Palace
candidates.price: Adult 2750 TL (combi for Palace, Harem and Hagia Irene)
candidates.content: The imperial enclave of the Ottoman emperors for four centuries. Lavishly decorated, with exhibitions of fine craftmanship and four courts of increasing grandeur. The second court has the Harem and the State Treasury, housing a we

candidates.name: Basilica Cistern
candidates.content: Vast underground cistern built by Justinian in 532 to store the city's water, the largest and best-known of the hundreds constructed. It's a cathedral-like space with 336 richly decorated columns. Time was you explored in a little

candidates.name: Museum of Archaeology
candidates.price: Adult €15. Beware of the ticket office staff adding the audio guide to the ticket price without asking if you want it. It's not compulsory and you don't need it. Check the bill before paying!
candidates.hours: Daily 09:00-17:30. The Tiled Kiosk and the Museum of Oriental Art are closed as of October 2025
candidates.content: Turkey was slow to protect its antiquities and to display them properly, but in 1867 Sultan Abdülaziz toured the museums of Paris, London and Vienna and saw what was needed. The main collection is in a grand neo-classical building

candidates.name: Museum of the History of Science and Technology in Islam
candidates.alt: İslam Bilim ve Teknoloji Tarihi Müzesi
candidates.content: Museum in a restored building that was the stables for Topkapı Palace. It exhibits various instruments for astronomy, clocks, pumps, weaponry, a steam-powered döner spit, and so on developed in Islamic realms down the centuries, b

candidates.name: Istanbul Railway Museum
candidates.content: Housed in the Europe-side railway terminus of 1890, this exhibits Ottoman and modern Turkish railway history. The Orient Express came and went from here, with passengers for further east transferring to ferries then the Asia-side

candidates.name: Little Hagia Sophia
candidates.content: Built as the Church of Saints Sergius and Bacchus around 530 AD, the same time as Hagia Sophia, but their styles differ. Transformed into a mosque in the early 1500s, it's beautifully decorated, with fine marble details, and has a

candidates.name: Theodosius Cistern
candidates.content: This was rediscovered in 2010 when an overlying building was demolished. It was built circa 430 AD to store water brought in by Valens Aqueduct. It's smaller than the better-known Basilica Cistern, but better lit, more atmospheric

candidates.name: Molla Zeyrek Mosque
candidates.content: This is a triple structure: the church of the Monastery of Pantokrator built 1118, then a public church circa 1136 plus a chapel that served as a royal mausoleum. It became a mosque and medresse in Ottoman times, but without massi

candidates.name: Cağaloğlu Hamamı
candidates.content: Built in 1741, the last major hamam opened in the Ottoman era. It has ornate architecture, great service and a stellar cast of famous visitors. Prices to match, and only tourists now use it.

candidates.name: Süleymaniye Hamamı
candidates.content: Commissioned by Süleyman the Magnificent and built by Mimar Sinan in 1550, at the east edge of Süleymaniye mosque complex. It had private cubicles for distinguished visitors such as the sultan, but was mostly a standard working-cl

candidates.name: Maçka Park
candidates.content: This park occupies the sides of a valley of this "city of seven hills", with an avenue in the bottom. A 4-person gondola lift line is strung over it, offering a shortcut when walking between Beşiktaş and Taksim Square as well as n

candidates.name: Üsküdar Musical Society
candidates.content: Founded in 1918, the society is often considered the most respected of the social clubs offering classes in the classical Ottoman music, and catching up with their frequent public concerts is certainly a good way of entering the v

candidates.name: Vialand
candidates.price: US$55, under 3 free, discount for domestic visitors
candidates.content: The only theme park of the city has a good selection of rides, including a couple of rollercoasters.

candidates.name: Hürrem Sultan Hamamı
candidates.content: Bathhouse built in 1556 by Mimar Sinan, the chief Ottoman architect, at the request of Hürrem Sultan (Roxelana), wife of Suleiman the Magnificent. It was built over the former public baths of Zeuxippus, abandoned around 713. Resto

candidates.name: Çemberlitaş Hamamı
candidates.content: Built in 1584, credited to Mimar Sinan but he probably only had light-touch supervision. It was astride the city's highway from Europe and very profitable, in spite of multiple earthquakes and fires. It fell out of use late 19th c

candidates.name: Galataport
candidates.content: It includes the city's cruise ship terminal, around 250 shops, pubs and restaurants, a Peninsula hotel, the Istanbul Modern art museum, and other cultural and entertainment facilities; the complex also hosts festivals.

candidates.name: Rami Library
candidates.content: 19th century barracks serving as municipality library.

candidates.name: Fenerbahçe SK
candidates.content: They play soccer in Süper Lig, the top tier, and routinely qualify for European tournaments. There's also a museum of the club, which fields teams in several other sports such as basketball.

candidates.name: Attend the Tataula Carnival
candidates.content: Despite a 1943 ban on this Greek Orthodox pre-Lent carnival by the Turkish authorities, it has been revived since 2010. The tradition began in the 19th century or earlier, and even though the event was led by local Greeks, the cel

candidates.name: The Sultan's Trail
candidates.content: A 2,500-km hiking and cycling trail stretching all the way to Vienna, retracing the campaign of Suleiman the Magnificent onto the Habsburg capital. It is not marked on the ground, but the GPS tracks are available through its websi

candidates.name: Tarihi Çinili Hamamı
candidates.content: Turkish bath cheaper than the more touristy ones in the European side.

candidates.name: Ülker Sports Arena
candidates.content: A multi-purpose arena for sports and concerts, owned by Fenerbahçe and home court of their basketball team. The museum displays their trophies.

candidates.name: Ataşehir Golf Club
candidates.content: It's only 9 holes, but one of the few golf clubs in the city.

candidates.name: Çekmeköy Nature Park
candidates.content: A bosky open space.

candidates.name: Beşiktaş Stadium
candidates.content: Homecourt of Beşiktaş JK

candidates.name: Şifa Hamamı
candidates.content: Established in 1777, this is one of the cheaper options. It's marble throughout and the fittings could be original. It has a mixed main section and a separate female section for the scrubbing.

candidates.name: Atatürk Olympic Stadium
candidates.content: An Olympic venue. Home court of the national team.

candidates.name: Black Sea Coast
candidates.content: There's a string of small coastal resorts, from Poyrazköy just beyond the north Bosphorus bridge, through Anadolufenerli, Riva. Usual beach attractions, but the Black Sea is often rough so beware of the waves. There is also a big

candidates.name: Vefa Bozacısı
candidates.content: Established in 1876, this cafe specializes in boza, a ferment of bulgur wheat with a sweetish tart taste. A favourite of the Ottomans, it's still popular in the Balkans and Central Asia. It's less than 1% alcohol, but it was the c

candidates.name: Kazan
candidates.content: A quite elegantly decorated local pub in which fans of Beşiktaş FC that could not make it to the stadium, old and young, male and female, like to watch the games on live broadcast. During summer months, they also have an open-air

candidates.name: Riddim Club Taksim
candidates.content: A complex with three floor. Rıddim live is the performance hall of complex and you can listen rock pop and alternative kinds of music. Riddim Special is the conceptual parties floor. İstanbul's best R&B-HipHop club is Rıddım R&B-H

candidates.name: Montreal Nevizade
candidates.content: Located in Nevizade where you can see so many small bars located next to each other, has live music and beer and shots in a subdued ambience of neon lights.

candidates.name: Mektup Bar
candidates.content: Authentic live music. But, there is a restaurant, too. Do expect to pay a cover charge (approximately 15 TL) if there is a band playing.

candidates.name: Snog Rooftop Bar
candidates.content: Good bar. But the attraction here is the stunning view.

candidates.name: Pierre Loti
candidates.content: An open air café on a hill overlooking the Golden Horn in Eyüp. It’s rumored that the French writer the place is named after used to love visiting this café during his residence in Istanbul. The cable car up here offers some nice

candidates.name: Karga
candidates.content: A finely decorated bar in a three-storey old building with wooden ceilings and floors. Also has a small yard at the back.

candidates.name: Ağaç Ev
candidates.content: Late spot for cocktails and live music.

candidates.name: Levent
candidates.content: A neighborhood which is just across the Sapphire of Istanbul and hosts nice bars.

candidates.name: Taps
candidates.content: A bar, restaurant and brewery in one. The crowd is the general Nişantaşı crowd, it also attracts a lot of expatriates.

candidates.name: Sayfiye Cocktail Bar
candidates.content: Temporarily closed.

candidates.name: Silivri Marina
candidates.content: There are cafes, pubs and restaurants along the pier.

candidates.name: İki 1A Kafası
candidates.content: Lively pub with music. It's near the university so it draws a student crowd.

candidates.name: Bereket Döner
candidates.price: 13-23 TL for a full meal; can be substantially cheaper if you forgo salad or appetizers
candidates.content: A quite good value restaurant featuring döner (also on the plate as opposed to the usual wrap/sandwich variety; dipped in tomato sauce to the point of swimming) and traditional Turkish cuisine. The restaurant is a self-service one

candidates.name: İbrahim Hakkı Uğrak Börek
candidates.content: A bit off the tourist track, the stone oven of this börek shop gives its products a distinctive flavour. Good value and friendly staff. Opens early, but not all varieties of börek will be ready first thing in the morning—the peyni

candidates.name: Ficcin
candidates.price: Around 20 TL per person without wine
candidates.content: The restaurant offers an exceptional value lunch, but is also pleasantly busy at night. Several of the staff speak English and foreign tourists are welcome alongside the many locals who eat there regularly. Fıccın is unusual in be

candidates.name: Akmanoğlu Fırını
candidates.content: This is the bakery where halkas mentioned in the "See" section, as well as a number of other traditional cookies, both sweet and salty, are produced and sold.

candidates.name: Ali Usta Çiğ Köfte
candidates.content: Good value Çiǧ köfte (spicy wrap with a vegan tatar) takeaway. Ali the owner is an Instagram celeb for his videos jibing customers, so you may be in a long line.

candidates.name: Kemerburgaz
candidates.content: A village (and nowadays a commuter suburb) at the edge of the forest, 15 km north of Eyüp and 10 km west of Bahçeköy. Several ancient aqueducts stand nearby, notably Kurt Kemeri ("Wolf's Aqueduct") and Uzun Kemer ("Long Aqueduct")

candidates.name: Kanaat Lokantası
candidates.content: Kanaat Lokantası, which dates back to 1933, is famous for its traditional Ottoman cuisine as well as a variety of fascinating desserts. The prices are reasonable but they accept nothing but cash.

candidates.name: Şampiyon Kokoreç
candidates.content: A restaurant mostly focused in kokoreç — roasted and finely minced lamb intestines (yeap). It tastes great and is very budget-friendly: only 10 TL/wrap. Try stuffed mussels as well.

candidates.name: Privato
candidates.price: Breakfast 65 TL per person, mains 30-40 TL
candidates.content: Traditional Turkish food with a focus on vegetarian dishes. Great for breakfast. Has a small patio in the back with a view of the Galata tower.

candidates.name: Buyruk Esnaf Lokantası
candidates.content: A place that serves home-made style foods ("ev yemekleri") which you can order from the counter. Great variety.

candidates.name: Sultana's Dinner and 1001 Nights Show
candidates.content: In Elmadag, near Taksim, has traditional Turkish cuisine (meze, kebabs, desserts) with a show every evening of belly dancing, Turkish folklore and live music.

candidates.name: Kosebasi Kebap
candidates.content: This Zagat-rated kebab joint serves traditional Turkish kebabs in modern/ upscale atmosphere. Levent is the main branch but they have 7 more locations (including 3 express versions) in Istanbul.

candidates.name: Beşiktaş Market
candidates.content: This is where locals go shopping. If you are keen to buy fruits, vegetables, walnuts or olives at local prices, this is where you should head. It is always a good idea to bring rome walnuts or olives back home. Otherwise it is jus

candidates.name: Paristexas Concept Store
candidates.content: Sertaç Haznedaroğlu, the fashion-forward owner, stocks quirky Japanese labels and rare collections created for an Eastern market by designers such as Marc Jacobs, Vivienne Westwood and Chloé. Also check out custom-made leather bag

candidates.name: Historia AVM
candidates.content: AVM (alışveriş merkezi) means a shopping mall, and Historia is the only one in the Old City. Usual selections of garments, electronics, furniture, a large supermarket, plus a bowling alley, fast food and a cinema. Across the alley

candidates.name: Yeşilköy (Green Village) Market
candidates.content: Far less chaotic market in the west with about 2,000 stalls to be explored.

december.text: Snowfall is somewhat common between December and March, however this changes quite a bit from year to year. Mild winters can get only a trace of accumulation, while colder winters can bring up to three weeks of snow cover. One other thing to note here is how heavy the snow can get in Istanbul. İncekum Adventure Park: Family-oriented activity centre.
